evidence.reason: Proposal workload entrypoint: enqueues a logFuture on applyCh; future completes with ErrNotLeader/ErrEnqueueTimeout/ErrLeadershipLost and exposes Index()/Response() through ApplyFuture (future.go).
Membership-change entrypoints: build a configurationChangeRequest and return an IndexFuture resolved by appendConfigurationEntry on the leader (raft.go:1203).
Completion contract for every workload call: Error() blocks until accepted/committed; Index()/Response() return the log index and FSM result.

external_input.boundary: Public Raft API and protocol state loops, Transport abstraction, InmemTransport, observer/future mechanisms, module-provided in-memory stores/snapshots, package-provided in-process testing support (excluding NetworkTransport/TCP sockets, external durable stores, application FSM semantics, process supervision, fuzzy/raft-compat/bench)
external_input.reason: Ordinary application workload entrypoints already exist as exported, documented, callable methods: proposal entrypoints Apply/ApplyLog and replicated membership-change entrypoints AddVoter/AddNonvoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter (plus deprecated AddPeer/RemovePeer for protocol versions <= 2). Completion is via the Future/IndexFuture/ApplyFuture contract (blocking Error(), Index(), Response()). Discovery-only capability: no target change needed.
limitations: Apply/Barrier/Restore accept caller deadlines (timeout duration) that only bound enqueue; they do not bound commit completion.
AddPeer/RemovePeer are deprecated and return ErrUnsupportedProtocol for ProtocolVersion > 2 (api.go:908-936).
Apply must run on the leader; followers get ErrNotLeader; mid-flight leadership loss yields ErrLeadershipLost with unknown write outcome (api.go:804-821).
external_input.test_support_reason: The entrypoints are exported, documented, and directly callable by the declared test consumer; completion semantics and result mechanisms (Future.Error/Index/Response) are public. Excluded per contract: BootstrapCluster (bootstrap), Restore (restore), Snapshot (administration), Barrier (barrier), VerifyLeader (leadership check), GetConfiguration (configuration query), LeadershipTransfer (administration), Stats/State/observer (observation).
execution_paths: proposal: Raft.Apply/ApplyLog([]byte|Log, timeout) -> applyCh -> dispatchLogs -> StoreLogs -> commit -> fsmMutateCh -> FSM.Apply -> ApplyFuture.Error()/Index()/Response()

membership change: Raft.AddVoter/AddNonvoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter(ServerID, ..., prevIndex, timeout) -> configurationChangeCh -> appendConfigurationEntry -> LogConfiguration dispatch/commit -> IndexFuture

evidence.reason: Peer-to-peer message ingress lives in the RPC handler, not in the workload entrypoint list.

protocol_ingress_excluded.reason: Only workload entrypoints (Apply/ApplyLog, membership APIs) are reported. Peer protocol ingress (processRPC dispatching AppendEntriesRequest/RequestVoteRequest/RequestPreVoteRequest/InstallSnapshotRequest/TimeoutNowRequest at raft.go:1390-1413) is explicitly excluded.

evidence.reason: Timers are internal loop mechanisms and are excluded from external_input.

timer_and_internal_events_excluded.reason: No timer, callback, or internal event is listed as a workload entrypoint; heartbeatTimer/electionTimer and notification channels are internal mechanisms.

evidence.reason: Command proposal from application code, replicated through the Raft log.
Membership change request replicated as a LogConfiguration entry.

workload_entrypoint.reason: Application-originating work is identified: replicated commands (Apply/ApplyLog) and replicated membership-change requests (AddVoter/AddNonvoter/RemoveServer/DemoteVoter).

evidence.reason: Every in-boundary cross-node RPC is delivered to Raft exclusively through trans.Consumer(); Raft sets rpcCh: trans.Consumer() in NewRaft (api.go:561), so a decorator wrapping the transport owns all continuation.

All synchronous sends (AppendEntries, RequestVote, RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot, TimeoutNow) and pipelined sends (inmemPipeline.AppendEntries, line 311) place an RPC into the peer's consumerCh; responses return via RPC.RespChan created here (line 177), which the decorator must swap to capture responses.

Normal ingress: the main loop consumes RPC from rpcCh and calls rpc.Respond (transport.go:25) to complete the original caller; capturing before delivery and injecting the same RPC keeps the exchange completion mechanism intact.

There is no single common concrete message struct for requests and responses; all commands implement WithRPCHeader, so a target-native typed variant carrier must be added for PendingMessage.Message (allowed by contract).

message_capture.boundary: Logical cross-node protocol messages inside system_boundary: requests, responses and one-way messages flowing over the Transport abstraction between *Raft nodes (InmemTransport in scope; NetworkTransport/TCP sockets out of scope)
message_capture.gap: Missing: MessageController/MessageHandle/PendingMessage/MessageKind surface; request retention before delivery with controller-owned continuation; response capture (requires RespChan swap at capture time); InstallSnapshot io.Reader replayable buffering; typed common message carrier; deep-copy at both producer->controller and controller->Pending boundaries; thread-safe cache that never evicts.
message_capture.reason: No MessageController exists, but the lowest shared typed boundary (Transport.Consumer() <-chan RPC consumed by Raft.rpcCh at NewRaft) is a complete interception seam: a Transport decorator (adapter) can own the Consumer channel, hold RPCs before delivery, and swap rpc.RespChan at capture so responses are also intercepted and later injected into the preserved original RespChan. This preserves protocol semantics and production defaults (no controller configured => pure forwarding), so the missing controller surface is addable without protocol, persistence, or state-transition changes.
limitations: Heartbeat fast-path: transports implementing SetHeartbeatHandler (NetworkTransport, out of boundary) can bypass Consumer; in-scope InmemTransport ignores SetHeartbeatHandler (inmem_transport.go:74), so in-boundary capture is complete, but the decorator must also intercept SetHeartbeatHandler for out-of-boundary transports.

Drop of a captured request leaves the original sender blocked on RespChan until the transport timeout ('command timed out', inmem_transport.go:196); under virtual time this timeout must be resolved by the decorator on the Drop path.
InstallSnapshot requests carry a one-shot stream (RPC.Reader); capture must buffer it into independently replayable storage before delivery and release it when the entry leaves the cache.
Source/Target identity: ServerID/ServerAddress (configuration.go:59-61); RPCHeader.ID/Addr supply the sender; Target is the receiving node's local identity.
message_capture.test_support_reason: Only primitives exist: the Transport interface and per-node consumer channels. Nothing retains messages before delivery, there is no response-visible seam (responses bypass Consumer via RPC.RespChan), and the package's cluster harness (MakeCluster) returns the unexported *cluster type, so external consumers cannot use it. A controller and Transport decorator must be written.
suggested_changes: Add MessageController (NewMessageController), MessageHandle (struct backed by unexported uint64), PendingMessage{Handle, Source ServerID, Target ServerID, Kind MessageKind, Message <typed carrier>}, Pending() []PendingMessage, Drop(handle) error, Clear() in a new exported package (adapter) or the raft package.

Add a Transport decorator (e.g., CapturingTransport) implementing Transport + WithPreVote + WithClose + WithPeers, owning the Consumer channel: read RPCs from the wrapped InmemTransport, deep-copy commands (field-wise/msgpack round-trip), buffer RPC.Reader into memory/bytes.Buffer, swap rpc.RespChan with the controller's channel, and record one pending entry per concrete target (broadcast fans out naturally because each per-peer RPC arrives at its own target consumer).

Add a typed variant carrier (one struct with a field per command type, or an interface with typed accessors) since no common concrete message struct exists; keep Pending copies independent and stream storage released on Drop/Clear/Inject.

For responses, record a second pending entry with reversed Source/Target and a new MessageHandle when rpc.Respond fires on the swapped channel; on Inject deliver RPCResponse into the preserved original RespChan so the original caller completes normally.
execution_paths: append_entries (incl. heartbeat): leader replicate()/heartbeat()/pipelineReplicate() -> Transport.AppendEntries or AppendEntriesPipeline -> peer consumerCh -> decorator Consumer -> Raft.processRPC -> AppendEntriesResponse via RespChan
request_vote: candidate electSelf() -> Transport.RequestVote -> peer consumerCh -> processRPC(requestVote) -> RequestVoteResponse via RespChan
request_prevote: candidate preElectSelf() -> Transport.RequestPreVote -> peer consumerCh -> processRPC(requestPreVote) -> RequestPreVoteResponse via RespChan
install_snapshot: leader sendLatestSnapshot() -> Transport.InstallSnapshot (+ data stream) -> consumerCh -> processRPC(installSnapshot) -> InstallSnapshotResponse via RespChan
timeout_now: leader leadershipTransfer() -> Transport.TimeoutNow -> consumerCh -> processRPC(timeoutNow) -> TimeoutNowResponse via RespChan

evidence.reason: The RPC struct carries the command, stream, and RespChan; Respond is the completion mechanism the controller must preserve and reuse on Inject.
The sender blocks on respCh (buffered 1) after enqueueing; injecting the held RPC later lets the normal handler respond, proving the original caller is not orphaned.
Raft consumes only trans.Consumer(); delivering a captured request into that channel is the same-path normal ingress for requests, responses, and one-way messages.

message_injection.boundary: Injection through the same in-boundary logical message routes (per-node Transport consumer -> Raft.processRPC -> RPC.Respond), using controller-owned cached entries
message_injection.gap: Missing: MessageController.Inject(handle) error; handle validity tracking (stable while pending, invalid after Drop/Clear/successful Inject); acceptance semantics (channel-send success removes the entry; failure preserves it); classified errors for not-pending, target-unavailable, and not-accepted.
message_injection.reason: Inject is implementable as a controller method that delivers the controller-owned RPC (request) into the owning node's consumer channel (r.rpcCh) - the normal protocol ingress - or delivers the captured response into the preserved original RespChan. Queue acceptance (buffered channel send) is the target's confirmed acceptance; failure preserves the entry. No protocol semantics change is needed, so the missing Inject surface and error classification are patchable.
limitations: Raft's consumer channel is unbuffered (make(chan RPC) at api.go:561 via trans.Consumer()); Inject's send can block until the main loop selects, so acceptance is the send itself - no separate ack exists; this matches 'queue acceptance is sufficient'.
The target cannot distinguish acceptance from later protocol failure; per contract the controller must not restore an injected entry, so a later failure never duplicates delivery.
For responses, Inject must route into the swapped-capture channel of the RPC the controller owns (i.e., the entry's stored RespChan), not into the consumer channel.
message_injection.test_support_reason: No Inject-like API exists; the underlying primitive is only a channel send into consumerCh. The full fixed surface (Inject(handle MessageHandle) error, ErrMessageNotPending/ErrTargetUnavailable/ErrMessageNotAccepted, cache-update semantics, handle invalidation) must be added.
suggested_changes: Add MessageController.Inject(handle MessageHandle) error performing the same-path delivery: for request entries, send the controller-owned RPC into the owning node's consumer channel; for response entries, send RPCResponse into the preserved original RespChan.

Define ErrMessageNotPending, ErrTargetUnavailable, ErrMessageNotAccepted as sentinel errors usable with errors.Is; on any failure return the error and keep the cache entry and handle intact; on successful send remove the entry and invalidate the handle.

Wire the controller's per-node decorators so Inject resolves the concrete target node (ServerID) that owns the entry; document that Inject returns after acceptance (enqueue), not after processing, commit, or response.
execution_paths: append_entries (incl. heartbeat): Inject -> owning node consumer channel -> processRPC(appendEntries) -> AppendEntriesResponse -> original RespChan
request_vote: Inject -> consumer channel -> processRPC(requestVote) -> RequestVoteResponse -> original RespChan
request_prevote: Inject -> consumer channel -> processRPC(requestPreVote) -> RequestPreVoteResponse -> original RespChan
install_snapshot: Inject (with replayed stream) -> consumer channel -> processRPC(installSnapshot) -> InstallSnapshotResponse -> original RespChan
timeout_now: Inject -> consumer channel -> processRPC(timeoutNow) -> TimeoutNowResponse -> original RespChan

evidence.reason: Single funnel for election/heartbeat/commit/snapshot/heartbeat-interval timers; returns time.After(minVal + rand extra) - the site that must be virtualized.
Protocol timers: heartbeatTimer (163, 217), electionTimer (310, 353), leader lease (677, 947) and leadership-transfer ElectionTimeout waits (728, 749) drive state transitions.
CommitTimeout re-arms (169, 495) and heartbeat interval (402) plus backoff waits (213, 419) schedule replication activity; virtual time must fire these in order.
Snapshot-interval timer (randomTimeout(SnapshotInterval)) controls autonomous snapshot work.

In-boundary transport timeouts (send/command timeouts, 500ms default) gate RPC completion and feed back into replication backoff and leader step-down; a virtual clock must cover them for full manual control.
r.run/r.runFSM/r.runSnapshots start immediately after NewRaft; the clock hook must be installed before NewRaft to close the uncontrolled window for external consumers.

time_control.boundary: Protocol time inside system_boundary: election/heartbeat/commit/lease timers in the *Raft state loops and replication goroutines, snapshot-interval timer, and InmemTransport RPC timeouts that feed back into protocol behavior (backoff, step-down)
time_control.gap: Missing: injectable clock/timer hooks in util.go/raft.go/replication.go/snapshot.go/inmem_transport.go; TimeController with Advance(steps uint64) error; install-before-NewRaft wiring; exclusion of caller-provided Apply/Barrier/Restore deadlines.
time_control.reason: No clock abstraction or Tick exists: all protocol time is direct time.After/time.Now (util.go randomTimeout; raft.go runFollower/runCandidate/leaderLoop; replication.go; snapshot.go; inmem_transport.go). A narrow no-op-by-default core hook (package-level injectable now/after functions) used by these sites, plus an exported TimeController with NewTimeController(...) and Advance(steps uint64) wired per *Raft and installed before NewRaft starts goroutines (api.go:622-624), preserves ordering, transition conditions, and production defaults. Missing Tick across files is not invasive here.
limitations: Caller-provided deadlines (Apply/Barrier/Restore timeouts, api.go:831/863/1060) are excluded per contract; requestConfigChange timeout (raft.go:118) is also caller-facing.
time.Now() reads used for lastContact/leader lease (raft.go:1036-1081, 1956-1960; replication.go:129-133) must also be virtualized or the lease path never fires under a frozen clock.

emitLogStoreMetrics and snapshot-transfer monitors are informational and excluded, but they also call time.After/time.Since (log.go:180) and would keep running on real time; they do not feed protocol behavior.
InmemTransport timeouts must be virtualized too; otherwise a captured/held message pair can resolve via real 500ms timeouts and break determinism.
time_control.test_support_reason: There is no clock seam at all: time.After and time.Now are called directly in protocol code, the global math/rand timer staggering cannot be paused, and same-package tests only shorten durations via inmemConfig. An external consumer cannot control protocol time today.
suggested_changes: Introduce package-level hooks (e.g., vars afterFunc(d time.Duration) <-chan time.Time and nowFunc() time.Time defaulting to time.After/time.Now) and route randomTimeout plus every protocol timer site and lastContact/lease read through them (no-op by default => production unchanged).

Add exported TimeController and NewTimeController(...) wiring every controlled *Raft (and its in-boundary InmemTransport), with Advance(steps uint64) error advancing a shared virtual clock: each step fires all due timers in deadline order and re-arms timers caused by earlier steps; pending/inject/drop/observe/external-input never advance time.

Document that Advance returns after due events are submitted (timer channels signalled), not after processing, and that paused/stopped/crashed subjects receive no steps; install the controller (or set the hooks) before NewRaft.
execution_paths: per-node protocol time: follower heartbeat/election timer (runFollower), candidate election timer (runCandidate), leader lease timer (leaderLoop), replication commit timer and heartbeat interval (replicate/heartbeat/pipelineReplicate), snapshot interval (runSnapshots), InmemTransport RPC timeouts - one shared controller per node, one step = one virtual-time unit advancing every running controlled subject without skipping intermediate due timers

evidence.reason: Single draw site: extra := time.Duration(rand.Int63()) % minVal; every election/heartbeat/commit/snapshot/heartbeat-interval re-arm draws here, so one hook controls all in-scope choices.
Global math/rand is seeded once from crypto/rand; there is no per-node source, so an external consumer cannot reproduce or observe draws today.
Call sites that consume randomTimeout for heartbeatTimer and electionTimer; the drawn duration is the semantic value to record (name + selected duration).

randomness_control.boundary: Hidden non-cryptographic protocol choices inside system_boundary: randomized timeout staggering drawn by randomTimeout in each *Raft node (election, heartbeat, commit, snapshot interval, heartbeat interval)
randomness_control.gap: Missing: injectable random source hook in randomTimeout; RandomController/RandomChoice/Choices() with deep-copied ordered history; install-before-first-draw wiring for external consumers (NewRaft starts goroutines immediately, api.go:622).
randomness_control.reason: The only in-scope hidden non-cryptographic choice is rand.Int63() inside randomTimeout (util.go:38), which randomizes every protocol timeout and directly affects election timing and test timing. It uses the global math/rand seeded once from crypto/rand with no injection seam. A narrow no-op-by-default core hook (injectable source for randomTimeout) plus RandomController(seed int64)/RandomChoice/Choices() is addable without changing semantics or the legal domain; generateUUID uses crypto/rand and is excluded.
limitations: generateUUID (util.go:59) uses crypto/rand and is excluded (peripheral identifiers/cryptography).
The recorded value is the selected timeout duration (semantic), not raw bits; random selection is separate from when the timer event fires (time_control owns firing).
Only one draw per timer re-arm; there are no other in-scope non-cryptographic choices in the module (fuzzy/ subdirectory is outside the boundary).
randomness_control.test_support_reason: No random-control surface exists; math/rand global is package-private behavior. Same-package tests only shorten timeout ranges (inmemConfig, testing.go:24) and cannot fix a seed or observe draws from outside.
suggested_changes: Add a package-level hook (e.g., var timeoutRand func() int64 defaulting to rand.Int63) used only by randomTimeout; production default unchanged.

Add exported RandomController with NewRandomController(seed int64, owner ...ServerID), Choices() []RandomChoice returning deep copies of {Name string, Value <typed duration/index>}, recording each draw in order with per-node owner attribution (or one controller per node).
Install the hook/controller before NewRaft so no uncontrolled draw can occur; same seed and draw order must reproduce the sequence, and repeated decisions draw the next value.
execution_paths: per-node randomized timeout draws: randomTimeout in runFollower (heartbeat), runCandidate (election), replicate/pipelineReplicate (commit), heartbeat (interval), runSnapshots (snapshot interval) - one RandomController per *Raft node

evidence.reason: Normal stop: closes shutdownCh, sets Shutdown state, returns shutdownFuture; Error() waits for all goroutines (future.go:171-180) and closes the transport when it implements WithClose.

waitShutdown() (state.go:153-155) blocks until every goFunc goroutine exits; transport Close is invoked for WithClose transports - the stop boundary, and the reason Restart must re-Connect InmemTransport peers.

Restart/recovery boundary: restores current term, last log, snapshot, and configuration from LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore before starting goroutines (restoreSnapshot at 631, config scan at 597-608).

Goroutines that do not select on shutdownCh: they block in transport RPC waits; Crash must force-resolve in-flight RPCs (e.g., disconnect/close in-boundary transport) so no abandoned context survives after Crash returns.
All raft-owned goroutines are tracked in routinesGroup; a core-hook crash path can reuse this to guarantee termination.
Target's own evidence of the stop-then-restart pattern: shutdown keeps data, fresh NewRaft with same stores resumes; with InmemTransport, peers must be reconnected after WithClose.

lifecycle_control.boundary: The *Raft node runtime and its goroutines (main loop, runFSM, runSnapshots, per-follower replicate/heartbeat/pipeline goroutines) plus consumer-provided durable stores (LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore) as the persistence boundary
lifecycle_control.gap: Missing: Pause/Resume (no mechanism to suspend a running node without stopping it), Crash (no abrupt-stop API; Shutdown always closes the transport and is the graceful path), LifecycleController/NewLifecycleController/ErrLifecycleUnsupported surface.
lifecycle_control.reason: Stop and Restart are already supported through public API (Shutdown + fresh NewRaft over the same stores; pattern evidenced by RaftEnv.Shutdown/Restart). Pause/Resume and Crash have no existing surface and require narrow no-op-by-default core hooks (pause gates in the state loops and replication goroutines; a crash termination path closing shutdownCh without transport close and resolving in-flight RPC waits). None of these change protocol, persistence, state-transition, or ordering semantics, so the capability is patchable; core hooks must be disclosed.
limitations: After Shutdown, InmemTransport is closed (DisconnectAll); Restart must re-Connect peers (cluster.FullyConnect pattern, testing.go:518).

Crash must resolve in-flight transport RPC goroutines (electSelf askPeer, inmemPipeline decodeResponses) so 'no abandoned execution context' holds; with a frozen virtual clock these would otherwise never complete.

Raft persists term and vote eagerly (raft.go:2141-2147, persistVote at 2130), so 'no extra protocol-state flush on crash' is naturally satisfied; only state already written to LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore survives.

The package's cluster harness (MakeCluster) returns the unexported *cluster type, so external consumers must assemble nodes manually (NewRaft + NewInmemTransport + NewInmemStore + FileSnapTest-equivalent).
lifecycle_control.test_support_reason: Stop and Restart are directly usable (Shutdown + NewRaft), but the five-operation LifecycleController surface (Pause/Resume/Crash/Restart with ErrLifecycleUnsupported classification) does not exist, and Pause/Resume/Crash have no public seam.
suggested_changes: LifecycleController with Pause(target *Raft)/Resume(target)/Stop(target)/Crash(target)/Restart(target) error, NewLifecycleController(...), and ErrLifecycleUnsupported (errors.Is-classifiable).

Pause/Resume: core_hook - add a per-node paused gate (e.g., pauseCh checked in runFollower/runCandidate/leaderLoop/runFSM/runSnapshots/replicate/heartbeat selects, no-op by default) that retains the same runtime and volatile state while blocking message handling, time steps, and output.

Stop: facade over Raft.Shutdown() (document transport close and peer re-connect on restart); Restart: facade constructing a fresh *Raft via NewRaft with same LocalID/config/stores (re-Connect InmemTransport peers) - post-stop state after Stop, pre-crash durable state after Crash.

Crash: core_hook - an abrupt-termination path that closes shutdownCh without transport close or state flush, resolves in-flight RPC waits (disconnect/close in-boundary transport), waits on routinesGroup, and discards the runtime; propose ErrLifecycleUnsupported if any operation cannot be implemented safely instead of fabricating it.

Ensure pending MessageController entries and deterministic control state (virtual clock, random history) survive lifecycle changes since they are controller-owned, and that fresh subjects are re-wired to all active controllers on Restart.
execution_paths: Stop -> Restart: Raft.Shutdown() (waits for goroutines, closes WithClose transport) -> durable stores retain term/log/snapshot/config -> fresh NewRaft with same LocalID, stores, re-connected transport
Crash -> Restart: core-hook abrupt termination (close shutdownCh without transport close/state flush, resolve in-flight RPC waits, discard *Raft) -> fresh runtime over pre-crash durable state only

Pause/Resume on same runtime: core-hook pause gates in runFollower/runCandidate/leaderLoop/runFSM/runSnapshots/replicate/heartbeat (no message handling, no time progress, no output; volatile state retained)

evidence.reason: Only shutdown mechanism; classified as Stop, not Crash, because shutdownFuture.Error also closes WithClose transports and is the documented graceful path.
Goroutines blocked in transport RPC waits that do not select on shutdownCh; Crash must resolve them to satisfy the no-abandoned-context requirement.

crash_boundary.reason: The boundary is identifiable (discard the *Raft runtime and volatile state; retain only store contents; no shutdown-time flush because raft persists eagerly), but no public API implements abrupt termination: Shutdown is the graceful path and closes the transport via WithClose (future.go:176-178). A core_hook crash method closing shutdownCh without transport close plus in-flight RPC resolution is required.

evidence.reason: Normal stop entrypoint returning a future that blocks until all background routines exit.
Waits on waitShutdown and performs target-defined cleanup (WithClose).

normal_stop_boundary.reason: Raft.Shutdown() is normal shutdown: closes shutdownCh, sets Shutdown state, waits for all goroutines, and optionally closes the transport; durable stores retain state for later restart.

evidence.reason: Loop blocks only on rpcCh/applyCh/verifyCh/timers/notifyCh/shutdownCh; nothing can hold it without stopping or changing these channels.

pause_resume_boundary.reason: No Pause/Resume mechanism exists anywhere in the module (no symbol matches); all state loops select only on rpcCh, applyCh, verifyCh, timers, notification channels, and shutdownCh. Same-instance pause with retained volatile state requires new core hooks.

evidence.reason: Durable log boundary defined by interface; InmemStore is the in-boundary test implementation (inmem_store.go:14).
Term and vote are persisted to StableStore before in-memory update; no shutdown-time flush exists.

persistent_volatile_semantics_defined.reason: The target defines persistence through consumer-provided LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore interfaces; raft writes current term and votes eagerly, so durable-vs-volatile semantics are explicit and Crash can retain only store contents.

evidence.reason: Rebuilds protocol state from LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore before starting goroutines.
Target's own restart pattern: fresh transport + NewRaft with the same config/stores after Shutdown.

restart_or_recovery_boundary.reason: Normal recovery is NewRaft over the same stores (term, last log, snapshot restore, configuration scan) plus the target's bootstrap/recover primitives; the same identity and configuration restart through conf.LocalID.

evidence.reason: logs/stable/snapshots/trans are injected dependencies; protocol state lives in the Raft object and raftState.
Volatile protocol state (term cache, commit/applied indices, last log/snapshot cache, state) with atomic/mutex access.

state_ownership_defined.reason: Raft owns in-memory protocol state (raftState in state.go, leaderState, configurations) and goroutines; durable state is owned by the consumer-supplied LogStore/StableStore/SnapshotStore; no cross-subsystem ownership ambiguity.

evidence.symbol: Raft.State / Stats / CurrentTerm / CommitIndex / AppliedIndex / LeaderWithID / LastContact / GetConfiguration
evidence.reason: Typed, lock- or atomic-backed getters returning node role, term, commit/applied indices, last index, leader identity, last contact, and configuration (Configuration future with Clone at configuration.go:83).
getState/getCurrentTerm/getCommitIndex/getLastApplied use atomic loads - thread-safe, side-effect-free, no time advancement.
Typed event stream (Data field carries RaftState, RequestVoteRequest, PeerObservation, LeaderObservation, Failed/ResumedHeartbeatObservation) with filter and blocking options.
The consumer already owns the store it passed to NewRaft and can read committed log ranges; returns a value copy (*log = *l).

observation.boundary: Per-*Raft-node typed state views and the observer mechanism inside system_boundary (no cross-node global snapshot promised)
observation.reason: Existing safe typed status APIs fully satisfy per-subject observation: State()/CurrentTerm()/CommitIndex()/AppliedIndex()/LastIndex() are atomic loads (state.go), Stats() builds a fresh string map, GetConfiguration() returns a cloned Configuration through a future, and the exported Observer mechanism delivers typed events (RaftState, LeaderObservation, PeerObservation, Failed/ResumedHeartbeatObservation, RequestVoteRequest). All are thread-safe, side-effect-free, and do not advance time; no new accessor is needed.
limitations: Separate getters are read independently; there is no simultaneous multi-field or multi-node snapshot - disclose temporal inconsistency.
GetConfiguration returns the latest (possibly uncommitted) configuration (api.go:897); Stats() labels it 'latest_configuration'.
AppliedIndex reflects entries sent to the FSM channel, not necessarily consumed by the application FSM (api.go:1238-1247).

MockFSM.Logs()/configurations are exported but documented as 'not a stable API' (testing.go:36-107); the cluster harness (MakeCluster) returns the unexported *cluster type and is unusable outside the package.

observation.test_support_reason: All required observations (role, term, commit_index, applied_index, log ranges via the owned store) are available through exported, documented, thread-safe APIs; no controller or snapshot schema is needed.
execution_paths: per-node status views: State/Stats/CurrentTerm/CommitIndex/AppliedIndex/LastIndex/LeaderWithID/LastContact/GetConfiguration/observer channel, each read independently (no simultaneous cross-subject freeze)
